ei.title: The Mosquito: The Worst Bug on the Planet?
ei.subject: 공통영어2

fullPassage: The Mosquito: The Worst Bug on the Planet? PART 1 - THE NUISANCE You are on a camping trip with your family or friends. After a long day of hiking, you take a quick shower, sit in your favorite camping chair, pick up a soda, and let out a deep, contented sigh. Right at that moment, you hear that annoying and familiar buzzing sound. Beating its wings as fast as 600 times per second, a mosquito sneaks in and pierces your skin with its straw-like mouthparts. Next, it fills its belly with blood and then escapes quickly, leaving behind an itchy red bump. This is a mild allergic reaction to the mosquito’s saliva. The more you scratch the bump, the more it itches. But how do mosquitoes find their victims anyway? Carbon dioxide, which humans and other animals breathe out, is actually a key signal to mosquitoes that a nice meal is near. They are highly sensitive to CO₂ and can detect it from far away. That’s not the only cue they use to find their victims. When you sweat, you release certain chemicals that attract them. Moreover, they can easily notice that your body temperature has risen. Why do they want our blood in the first place? It turns out that only females bite us; they need protein to produce eggs. If our blood did not contain protein, they would not bother us. After the mosquito successfully takes a blood meal of up to three times her own body weight, she quickly lands on the nearest vertical surface. With the aid of gravity, she drains off the water from the blood she took. Using this concentrated blood, she develops her eggs over the next few days. She then lays roughly 200 floating eggs on the surface of a small pool of water. PART 2 - THE PREDATOR If you had to choose our greatest predator in nature, which would you pick? Sharks, lions, or bears? According to history professor Timothy Winegard, it is actually the mosquito. Mosquitoes can pass on deadly diseases like malaria and yellow fever. Over a million people worldwide die of these diseases every year. Throughout history, Winegard estimates that mosquitoes have killed more people than any other single cause — about fifty-two billion people, nearly half of all humans who have ever lived. Winegard claims that mosquitoes also played a role in shaping the history of several countries. Take the Roman Empire, for example. The fall of the Western Roman Empire was gradual, spanning over centuries. Here are commonly cited reasons for the fall of the empire: invasions by outside forces, economic troubles, and corruption. Diseases like malaria, however, also contributed. Rome, the capital of the empire, was once surrounded by a huge stretch of wetland. This was an ideal breeding ground for mosquitoes and hence a hot spot for malaria. On the one hand, mosquitoes helped protect the city against the armies coming to attack it. However, they eventually spread the disease not only throughout the city, but also throughout the empire, crushing much of the population. Here is another reason why Winegard considers the mosquito a powerful agent of historical change. In 1698, five ships set sail from Scotland, carrying twelve hundred settlers and valuable trade goods. They headed for the Darien region of Panama, where Scotland planned to create a trading center. After struggling through years of a food crisis, Scotland had hoped this would help raise its economic prospects. The ambitious plan, however, was brought down by the local diseases: yellow fever and malaria. Virtually no one from Scotland had ever encountered any of these diseases before. After six months, nearly half of them died, and the survivors returned to their ships and fled. If their immune systems had been much stronger, they would not have lost so many lives in such a short time. Surprisingly, human beings lived with and died of these diseases for thousands of years without understanding how they were spread. It was not until the end of the nineteenth century that we found out that mosquitoes spread malaria. Before this finding, no one imagined that these tiny annoying insects might be affecting our lives so deeply. Now we all know that human history is not free from the workings of the natural world.

questions.passage: The more you scratch the bump, the more it itches.  But how do mosquitoes find their victims anyway?  Carbon dioxide, ①<u>which</u> humans and other animals breathe out, is actually a key signal to mosquitoes that a nice meal is near.  They are highly sensitive to CO₂ and can detect it from far away.  That’s not the only cue they use ②<u>to find</u> their victims.  When you sweat, you release certain chemicals that ③<u>attracts</u> them.  Moreover, they can easily notice that your body temperature ④<u>has risen</u>.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ③ attracts → attract: 앞의 명사가 certain chemicals(여러 화학 물질, 복수)라서 동사도 복수형 attract
det.analysis:
① which: 'Carbon dioxide, which humans and other animals breathe out, is~'에서 콤마 뒤 which는 앞의 Carbon dioxide(이산화탄소)를 받아 '그런데 그것은 사람과 동물이 내뿜는 것인데'라고 이어 주는 관계대명사예요. 사물을 받으니 which가 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

② to find: 'the only cue they use to find their victims'는 '먹잇감을 찾기 위해 사용하는 유일한 단서'예요. '~하기 위해'라는 목적을 나타낼 때 to부정사(to find)를 쓰니 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

③ attracts → 여기가 정답(틀린 곳)! 'you release certain chemicals that attract them'은 '너는 그들(모기)을 끌어들이는 특정 화학 물질을 내보낸다'예요. that이 가리키는 것은 앞의 certain chemicals(화학 물질들, 복수)예요. 주어가 복수면 동사도 복수형이라 -s를 빼고 attract로 써야 해요. attracts는 단수 취급이라 틀려요. ❌ attracts는 틀림 ←정답

④ has risen: 'your body temperature has risen'은 '너의 체온이 (지금) 올라가 있다'예요. 방금 일어난 일이 지금까지 이어질 때 현재완료(has + 과거분사)를 쓰니 has risen이 맞아요. ✅ 올바름
det.tip: 관계대명사 that/which 뒤 동사는 앞의 명사(chemicals=복수)에 수를 맞춘다 → attract

questions.passage: Right at that moment, you hear that annoying and familiar buzzing sound.  ①<u>Beating</u> its wings as fast as 600 times per second, a mosquito sneaks in and ②<u>piercing</u> your skin with its straw-like mouthparts.  Next, it fills its belly with blood and then escapes quickly, ③<u>leaving</u> behind an itchy red bump.  This is a mild allergic reaction to the mosquito’s saliva.  The more you scratch the bump, the more it ④<u>itches</u>.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ② piercing → pierces: 앞의 sneaks in과 and로 나란히 이어지는 병렬 구조라 같은 형태인 pierces
det.analysis:
① Beating: 'Beating its wings as fast as 600 times per second, a mosquito sneaks in~'은 '날개를 초당 600번이나 퍼덕이면서, 모기가 몰래 들어온다'예요. 모기가 스스로 날개를 퍼덕이는 것(능동)이라 -ing형(Beating)으로 시작하는 분사구문이 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

② piercing → 여기가 정답(틀린 곳)! 원문은 'a mosquito sneaks in and pierces your skin'으로 '모기가 몰래 들어와서 네 피부를 찌른다'예요. 주어 a mosquito에 딸린 동사가 sneaks(들어온다)와 pierces(찌른다) 둘인데, and로 나란히 이어지면(병렬 구조) 형태를 똑같이 맞춰야 해요. sneaks가 -s형이니 짝도 pierces여야 하는데, piercing은 형태가 달라서 틀려요. ❌ piercing은 틀림 ←정답

③ leaving: 'it fills its belly with blood and then escapes quickly, leaving behind an itchy red bump'은 '피로 배를 채우고 재빨리 달아나면서, 가려운 붉은 자국을 남긴다'예요. 달아나는 동시에 자국을 남기는 상황이라 -ing형(leaving) 분사구문이 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

④ itches: 'The more you scratch the bump, the more it itches'는 '그 자국을 긁을수록, 그만큼 더 가렵다'예요. 주어 it(그 자국)은 단수라 동사에 -s를 붙여 itches로 쓰니 맞아요. ✅ 올바름
det.tip: and로 이어지는 두 동사는 형태를 똑같이: sneaks and pierces

questions.passage: After six months, nearly half of them died, and the survivors returned to their ships and fled.  If their immune systems ①<u>have been</u> much stronger, they would not have lost so many lives in such a short time.  Surprisingly, human beings lived with and died of these diseases for thousands of years without understanding how they ②<u>were spread</u>.  It was not until the end of the nineteenth century that we ③<u>found out</u> that mosquitoes spread malaria.  Before this finding, no one imagined that these tiny annoying insects ④<u>might be affecting</u> our lives so deeply.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ① have been → had been: 뒤에 would not have lost(가정법 과거완료 결과)가 오므로 if절도 had + 과거분사
det.analysis:
① have been → 여기가 정답(틀린 곳)! 원문은 'If their immune systems had been much stronger, they would not have lost so many lives'로 '만약 그들의 면역 체계가 훨씬 강했더라면, 그렇게 많은 목숨을 잃지 않았을 것이다'예요. 과거에 실제로 일어나지 않은 일을 상상할 때는 'If + had + 과거분사(과거완료) ~, would have + 과거분사'를 써요(가정법 과거완료). 뒤 문장이 would not have lost이니, if절도 had been이어야 짝이 맞아요. have been은 형태가 어긋나서 틀려요. ❌ have been은 틀림 ←정답

② were spread: 'without understanding how they were spread'는 '그것들(질병)이 어떻게 퍼졌는지도 모른 채'예요. 질병은 스스로 퍼뜨리는 게 아니라 '퍼뜨려지는' 대상이라, be동사+과거분사(were spread) 수동태가 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

③ found out: 'It was not until~ that we found out that mosquitoes spread malaria'는 '~에 이르러서야 비로소 모기가 말라리아를 퍼뜨린다는 것을 알아냈다'예요. 이미 지난 일이라 과거형 found out이 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

④ might be affecting: 'these tiny annoying insects might be affecting our lives'는 '이 작고 성가신 곤충들이 우리 삶에 영향을 주고 있을지도 모른다'예요. '~하고 있을지도 모른다'라는 뜻이라 조동사 might 뒤에 be -ing(진행)을 쓰니 맞아요. ✅ 올바름
det.tip: 가정법 과거완료: If + had p.p. ~, would have p.p. → had been / would not have lost

questions.passage: Diseases like malaria, however, also contributed.  Rome, the capital of the empire, was once surrounded by a huge stretch of wetland.  This was an ①<u>ideal</u> breeding ground for mosquitoes and hence a hot spot for malaria.  On the one hand, mosquitoes helped ②<u>protect</u> the city against the armies coming to attack it.  However, they eventually ③<u>spread</u> the disease not only throughout the city, but also throughout the empire, ④<u>saving</u> much of the population.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ④ saving → crushing: 질병을 퍼뜨려 인구 대부분을 '짓밟았다(파괴)'는 흐름이라 crushing이 맞음
det.analysis:
① ideal: 'This was an ideal breeding ground for mosquitoes'는 '이곳은 모기에게 이상적인 번식지였다'예요. 로마가 넓은 습지로 둘러싸여 모기가 살기 딱 좋았다는 흐름이라 자연스러워요. ✅ 적절

② protect: 'mosquitoes helped protect the city against the armies'는 '모기가 그 도시를 공격군으로부터 지키는 것을 도왔다'예요. 뒤에 '공격하러 오는 군대'가 나오니, 모기(말라리아)가 침입군을 막아 도시를 지켰다는 흐름이라 맞아요. ✅ 적절

③ spread: 'they eventually spread the disease not only throughout the city, but also throughout the empire'는 '그것들이 결국 도시뿐 아니라 제국 전역에 질병을 퍼뜨렸다'예요. 모기가 병을 옮겼다는 흐름이라 자연스러워요. ✅ 적절

④ saving → 여기가 정답(부적절한 곳)! 원문은 'crushing much of the population'으로 '인구의 상당 부분을 짓밟았다(파괴했다)'예요. 앞에서 질병을 제국 전역에 퍼뜨렸다고 했으니, 인구를 '구한(saving)' 게 아니라 '무너뜨린(crushing)' 것이어야 흐름이 맞아요. saving은 정반대라 문맥에 안 맞아요. ❌ 부적절 ←정답
det.tip: 질병을 퍼뜨림 → 인구를 짓밟다(crushing), 구하다(saving)가 아님

questions.passage: Here is another reason why Winegard considers the mosquito a powerful agent of historical change.  In 1698, five ships set sail from Scotland, carrying twelve hundred settlers and ①<u>worthless</u> trade goods.  They headed for the Darien region of Panama, where Scotland planned to create a trading center.  After struggling through years of a food crisis, Scotland had hoped this would help ②<u>raise</u> its economic prospects.  The ambitious plan, however, was ③<u>brought down</u> by the local diseases: yellow fever and malaria.  Virtually no one from Scotland had ever encountered any of these diseases before.  After six months, nearly half of them died, and the ④<u>survivors</u> returned to their ships and fled.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ① worthless → valuable: 무역 중심지를 세우려 실은 물품이라 '값진(valuable)' 교역품이어야 함
det.analysis:
① worthless → 여기가 정답(부적절한 곳)! 원문은 'carrying twelve hundred settlers and valuable trade goods'로 '1,200명의 정착민과 값진 교역품을 실은'이에요. 뒤에 '무역 중심지를 세워 경제를 살리려 했다'는 내용이 나오니, 배에 실은 것은 값진(valuable) 교역품이어야 자연스러워요. '가치 없는(worthless)' 물건을 무역을 위해 싣는 건 앞뒤가 안 맞아요. ❌ 부적절 ←정답

② raise: 'Scotland had hoped this would help raise its economic prospects'는 '스코틀랜드는 이것이 자국의 경제 전망을 끌어올리기를 바랐다'예요. 식량 위기를 겪은 뒤라 경제를 '살리려(raise)' 했다는 흐름이라 맞아요. ✅ 적절

③ brought down: 'The ambitious plan, however, was brought down by the local diseases'는 '그러나 그 야심 찬 계획은 현지의 질병들에 의해 무너졌다'예요. however(그러나)로 이어지며 계획이 실패했다는 흐름이라, '무너뜨리다(brought down)'가 맞아요. ✅ 적절

④ survivors: 'the survivors returned to their ships and fled'는 '생존자들은 배로 돌아가 달아났다'예요. 앞에서 거의 절반이 죽었다고 했으니, 남은 사람들을 '생존자(survivors)'라 부르는 게 맞아요. ✅ 적절
det.tip: 무역 중심지를 세우려 실은 물품 → 값진(valuable) 교역품, 가치 없는(worthless) 게 아님

questions.passage: The more you scratch the bump, the more it itches.  But how do mosquitoes find their victims anyway?  Carbon dioxide, which humans and other animals breathe out, is actually a __________ to mosquitoes that a nice meal is near.  They are highly sensitive to CO₂ and can detect it from far away.  That’s not the only cue they use to find their victims.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: ③ key signal(핵심 신호): 모기가 이산화탄소에 매우 민감해 멀리서도 감지하니, 이산화탄소는 먹이가 가까이 있다는 '핵심 신호'
det.analysis:
빈칸 문장: 'Carbon dioxide, which humans and other animals breathe out, is actually a ___ to mosquitoes that a nice meal is near'(사람과 동물이 내뿜는 이산화탄소는 사실 모기에게 좋은 먹이가 가까이 있다는 ___이다). 바로 뒤에 '모기는 이산화탄소에 매우 민감해서 멀리서도 감지할 수 있다'가 나와요. 즉 이산화탄소는 먹이를 찾게 해 주는 '핵심 신호'가 되어야 흐름이 맞아요.

❌ ① minor obstacle(사소한 장애물): 이산화탄소가 모기를 방해한다는 내용은 없어요.

❌ ② false alarm(잘못된 경보): 이산화탄소는 실제로 먹이를 알려 주는 정확한 단서라, '잘못된' 신호가 아니에요.

✅ ③ key signal(핵심 신호): 모기가 민감하게 감지해 먹이를 찾는다는 흐름과 딱 맞아요. ←정답

❌ ④ deadly poison(치명적인 독): 이산화탄소가 모기에게 독이 된다는 내용은 없어요.
det.tip: 뒤 문장 '이산화탄소에 매우 민감, 멀리서도 감지' → 먹이를 알려 주는 핵심 신호(key signal)

questions.passage: If their immune systems had been much stronger, they would not have lost so many lives in such a short time.  Surprisingly, human beings lived with and died of these diseases for thousands of years without understanding how they were spread.  It was not until the end of the nineteenth century that we found out that mosquitoes spread malaria.  Before this finding, no one imagined that these tiny annoying insects might be affecting our lives so deeply.  Now we all know that human history is not __________ the workings of the natural world.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: ② free from(~로부터 자유로운): '인간 역사는 자연의 작용으로부터 자유롭지 않다' = 자연이 역사에 영향을 준다
det.analysis:
빈칸 문장: 'Now we all know that human history is not ___ the workings of the natural world'(이제 우리 모두는 인간의 역사가 자연 세계의 작용으로부터 ___하지 않다는 것을 안다). 앞에서 작은 모기가 우리 삶에 깊이 영향을 준다고 했어요. 즉 인간 역사가 자연의 힘과 무관하지 않다, 자연에서 '자유롭지 않다'는 뜻이 되어야 해요.

❌ ① responsible for(~에 책임이 있는): '역사가 자연에 책임이 없다'는 어색하고 글의 결론과도 안 맞아요.

✅ ② free from(~로부터 자유로운): 'is not free from ~'은 '~에서 자유롭지 못하다 = ~의 영향을 받는다'예요. 자연이 역사를 좌우해 왔다는 글의 결론과 딱 맞아요. ←정답

❌ ③ curious about(~에 대해 궁금해하는): 역사가 무언가를 궁금해한다는 건 말이 안 돼요.

❌ ④ tired of(~에 싫증 난): 역사가 싫증 난다는 것도 문맥과 맞지 않아요.
det.tip: be not free from ~ = ~에서 자유롭지 못하다(=영향을 받는다)

questions.passage: Right at that moment, you hear that annoying and familiar buzzing sound.  Beating its wings as fast as 600 times per second, a mosquito sneaks in and pierces your skin with its straw-like mouthparts.  Next, it fills its belly with blood and then escapes quickly, leaving behind an itchy red bump.  This is a mild allergic reaction to the mosquito’s saliva.  The more you scratch the bump, the more it itches.  But how do mosquitoes find their victims anyway?  Carbon dioxide, which humans and other animals breathe out, is actually a key signal to mosquitoes that a nice meal is near.  They are highly sensitive to CO₂ and can detect it from far away.  That’s not the only cue they use to find their victims.  When you sweat, you release certain chemicals that attract them.  Moreover, they can easily notice that your body temperature has risen.  Why do they want our blood in the first place?
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.korean: ④ 원문 근거: This is a mild allergic reaction to the mosquito's saliva
det.analysis:
❌ ① 원문 'only females bite us'(오직 암컷만 우리를 문다)와 반대예요. 무는 것은 수컷이 아니라 암컷이에요.

questions.passage: The Mosquito: The Worst Bug on the Planet?  PART 1 - THE NUISANCE You are on a camping trip with your family or friends.  After a long day of hiking, you take a quick shower, sit in your favorite camping chair, pick up a soda, and let out a deep, contented sigh.  Right at that moment, you hear that annoying and familiar buzzing sound.  Beating its wings as fast as 600 times per second, a mosquito sneaks in and pierces your skin with its straw-like mouthparts.  Next, it fills its belly with blood and then escapes quickly, leaving behind an itchy red bump.  This is a mild allergic reaction to the mosquito’s saliva.  The more you scratch the bump, the more it itches.  But how do mosquitoes find their victims anyway?  Carbon dioxide, which humans and other animals breathe out, is actually a key signal to mosquitoes that a nice meal is near.  They are highly sensitive to CO₂ and can detect it from far away.  That’s not the only cue they use to find their victims.  When you sweat, you release certain chemicals that attract them.  Moreover, they can easily notice that your body temperature has risen.  Why do they want our blood in the first place?  It turns out that only females bite us; they need protein to produce eggs.  If our blood did not contain protein, they would not bother us.  After the mosquito successfully takes a blood meal of up to three times her own body weight, she quickly lands on the nearest vertical surface.  With the aid of gravity, she drains off the water from the blood she took.  Using this concentrated blood, she develops her eggs over the next few days.  She then lays roughly 200 floating eggs on the surface of a small pool of water.  PART 2 - THE PREDATOR If you had to choose our greatest predator in nature, which would you pick?  Sharks, lions, or bears?  According to history professor Timothy Winegard, it is actually the mosquito.  Mosquitoes can pass on deadly diseases like malaria and yellow fever.  Over a million people worldwide die of these diseases every year.  Throughout history, Winegard estimates that mosquitoes have killed more people than any other single cause — about fifty-two billion people, nearly half of all humans who have ever lived.  Winegard claims that mosquitoes also played a role in shaping the history of several countries.  Take the Roman Empire, for example.  The fall of the Western Roman Empire was gradual, spanning over centuries.  Here are commonly cited reasons for the fall of the empire: invasions by outside forces, economic troubles, and corruption.  Diseases like malaria, however, also contributed.  Rome, the capital of the empire, was once surrounded by a huge stretch of wetland.  This was an ideal breeding ground for mosquitoes and hence a hot spot for malaria.  On the one hand, mosquitoes helped protect the city against the armies coming to attack it.  However, they eventually spread the disease not only throughout the city, but also throughout the empire, crushing much of the population.  Here is another reason why Winegard considers the mosquito a powerful agent of historical change.  In 1698, five ships set sail from Scotland, carrying twelve hundred settlers and valuable trade goods.  They headed for the Darien region of Panama, where Scotland planned to create a trading center.  After struggling through years of a food crisis, Scotland had hoped this would help raise its economic prospects.  The ambitious plan, however, was brought down by the local diseases: yellow fever and malaria.  Virtually no one from Scotland had ever encountered any of these diseases before.  After six months, nearly half of them died, and the survivors returned to their ships and fled.  If their immune systems had been much stronger, they would not have lost so many lives in such a short time.  Surprisingly, human beings lived with and died of these diseases for thousands of years without understanding how they were spread.  It was not until the end of the nineteenth century that we found out that mosquitoes spread malaria.  Before this finding, no one imagined that these tiny annoying insects might be affecting our lives so deeply.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: ④ 성가신 해충에 그치지 않고, 질병을 옮겨 로마·스코틀랜드처럼 인류 역사를 바꿔 온 모기의 영향력이 글 전체의 핵심
det.analysis:
글은 앞부분에서 모기가 어떻게 사람을 물고 피를 빠는지(성가신 해충)를 설명하고, 뒷부분에서 모기가 말라리아 같은 병을 옮겨 로마 제국의 몰락과 스코틀랜드의 실패에 영향을 주는 등 '가장 무서운 포식자'로서 인류 역사를 바꿔 왔다고 말해요.

❌ ① 무는 과정과 가려움의 원리는 글의 앞부분 일부일 뿐, 글 전체를 대표하지 못해요.

❌ ② 로마·스코틀랜드의 '경제적' 원인이 아니라, 모기가 옮긴 '질병'의 영향이 핵심이에요.

❌ ③ 질병을 예방·치료하는 현대 의학 이야기는 글에 거의 나오지 않아요.

✅ ④ 단순한 해충을 넘어 인류 역사를 바꿔 온 모기의 영향력: 앞부분(해충)과 뒷부분(역사를 바꾼 포식자)을 모두 담아요. ←정답
det.tip: 앞(성가신 해충) + 뒤(역사를 바꾼 포식자)를 모두 아우르는 선지가 주제

로마 제국과 스코틀랜드가 쇠퇴하게 된 경제적 원인 분석

❌ ④ 질병을 사람에게 옮기는 모기들: 모기는 뒤 문장에 나오지만, 여기 they는 '퍼뜨려지는' 병(diseases)을 가리켜요.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: ④ drains off the water(물기를 빼낸다): 바로 뒤에서 '농축된 피(concentrated blood)'로 알을 키운다고 하므로, 물기를 빼내는 것
det.analysis:
빈칸 문장: 'With the aid of gravity, she ___ from the blood she took'(중력의 도움으로, 그녀는 빨아들인 피에서 ___). 바로 다음 문장에 'Using this concentrated blood, she develops her eggs'(이 농축된 피를 이용해 알을 키운다)가 나와요. 피가 '농축'되려면 물기를 빼내야 하니, 빈칸은 '물기를 빼낸다'가 되어야 해요.

❌ ① quickly digests all of it(재빨리 전부 소화한다): 피를 소화해 없앤다면 뒤에서 그 피로 알을 키운다는 내용과 안 맞아요.

❌ ② warms up the blood again(피를 다시 데운다): 피를 데운다는 내용은 없어요.

❌ ③ shares the blood with others(피를 다른 개체와 나눈다): 피를 나눈다는 내용은 없어요.

✅ ④ drains off the water(물기를 빼낸다): 뒤의 '농축된 피(concentrated blood)'와 딱 이어져요. ←정답
det.tip: 뒤 문장 'concentrated blood(농축된 피)' → 물기를 빼냈다는 단서

questions.passage: Diseases like malaria, however, also contributed.  Rome, the capital of the empire, was once surrounded by a huge stretch of wetland.  __________ and hence a hot spot for malaria.  On the one hand, mosquitoes helped protect the city against the armies coming to attack it.
questions.stem:
다음 우리말 뜻에 맞도록 주어진 단어를 모두 배열하여 문장을 완성하시오.

"이곳은 모기에게 이상적인 번식지였다." (8단어) (영어로) [조건] (1) an, breeding, for, ground, ideal, mosquitoes, This, was 를 모두 사용 (2) 정확히 8단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: This was an ideal breeding ground for mosquitoes
det.analysis:
'이곳은 ~였다'가 핵심이라 '주어(This) + 동사(was)'로 시작해요: This → was.

무엇이었는가 하면 '이상적인 번식지'예요. 셀 수 있는 명사(ground) 앞이라 관사 an을 먼저 놓고, 꾸미는 형용사들을 순서대로 놓아요: an → ideal(이상적인) → breeding(번식의) → ground(장소). 'breeding ground'는 '번식지'라는 굳어진 표현이에요.

마지막으로 '모기에게'는 for mosquitoes로 뒤에 붙여요: for → mosquitoes.

순서대로 이으면 This / was / an / ideal / breeding / ground / for / mosquitoes.
det.tip: 관사(an) + 형용사(ideal breeding) + 명사(ground) 순서 / breeding ground = 번식지

questions.wa: This was an ideal breeding ground for mosquitoes
accept: This was an ideal breeding ground for mosquitoes

questions.passage: Take the Roman Empire, for example.  The fall of the Western Roman Empire was gradual, spanning over centuries.  Here are commonly cited reasons for the fall of the empire: invasions by outside forces, economic troubles, and corruption.  Diseases like malaria, however, also contributed.  Rome, the capital of the empire, was once ①<u>surrounding</u> by a huge stretch of wetland.  This was an ideal breeding ground for mosquitoes and hence a hot spot for malaria.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①은 어법상 틀렸다. 어법에 맞게 올바른 형태로 고쳐 쓰시오. (한 단어, 영어로)

det.korean: surrounding → surrounded: 로마는 '둘러싸는' 것이 아니라 '둘러싸이는' 대상이라 수동태 was + 과거분사(surrounded)
det.analysis:
밑줄이 있는 문장은 'Rome, the capital of the empire, was once ①<u>surrounding</u> by a huge stretch of wetland'이에요. '제국의 수도 로마는 한때 넓은 습지로 둘러싸여 있었다'라는 뜻이에요.

여기서 로마(Rome)는 습지를 둘러싸는 주체가 아니라, 습지에 '둘러싸이는' 대상이에요. 이렇게 '~되다/~당하다'를 나타낼 때는 수동태 'be동사 + 과거분사(p.p.)'를 써요.

surround(둘러싸다)의 과거분사는 surrounded예요. 그래서 'was surrounding'이 아니라 'was surrounded(둘러싸였다)'로 고쳐야 맞아요.

바로 뒤 'by a huge stretch of wetland(넓은 습지에 의해)'라는 표현도 이 문장이 수동태임을 알려 줘요. 'be동사 + p.p. + by ~'는 대표적인 수동태 형태예요.
det.tip: 수동태 be + 과거분사: was surrounded by ~ (~에 의해 둘러싸이다)

questions.passage: The ambitious plan, however, was brought down by the local diseases: yellow fever and malaria.  Virtually no one from Scotland had ever encountered any of these diseases before.  After six months, nearly half of them died, and the survivors returned to their ships and fled.  If their immune systems had been much stronger, __________ in such a short time.
questions.stem:
다음 우리말 뜻에 맞도록 주어진 단어를 모두 배열하여 문장을 완성하시오.

"그들은 그렇게 많은 목숨을 잃지는 않았을 것이다." (8단어) (영어로) [조건] (1) have, lives, lost, many, not, so, they, would 를 모두 사용 (2) 정확히 8단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: they would not have lost so many lives
det.analysis:
'그들은 ~하지 않았을 것이다'는 과거에 실제로 일어나지 않은 일을 상상하는 표현이에요. 이럴 때 결과 부분은 'would + have + 과거분사(가정법 과거완료)'를 써요.

먼저 주어와 조동사: they(그들은) + would(~였을 것이다).

부정은 would 바로 뒤에 not을 넣어요: would → not.

그다음 'have + 과거분사'로 '~했을'을 만들어요. lose(잃다)의 과거분사는 lost예요: have → lost.

무엇을 잃었는가 하면 'so many lives(그렇게 많은 목숨)'예요. so(그렇게) → many(많은) → lives(목숨들).

순서대로 이으면 they / would / not / have / lost / so / many / lives.
det.tip: 가정법 과거완료 결과절: would + not + have + p.p.(lost) / so many + 복수명사(lives)

questions.wa: they would not have lost so many lives
accept: they would not have lost so many lives

questions.passage: Diseases like malaria, however, also contributed.  Rome, the capital of the empire, was once surrounded by a huge stretch of wetland.  This was an ideal breeding ground for mosquitoes and hence a hot spot for malaria.  On the one hand, __________ coming to attack it.
questions.stem:
다음 우리말에 맞도록 주어진 단어를 올바른 순서로 배열하시오.
"모기는 그 도시를 공격해 오는 군대로부터 지키는 것을 도왔다."

[ against / armies / city / helped / mosquitoes / protect / the / the ] (8단어) (영어로)

det.korean: mosquitoes helped protect the city against the armies
det.analysis:
우리말 '모기는 ~하는 것을 도왔다'를 영어 어순으로 놓아요.

먼저 주어와 동사: mosquitoes(모기는) + helped(도왔다).

동사 help는 뒤에 동사원형을 바로 붙여 'help + 동사원형(~하는 것을 돕다)'을 만들어요: helped → protect(지키다).

무엇을 지키는가 하면 목적어 'the city(그 도시)'예요: the → city.

'~로부터, ~에 맞서'는 against로 나타내고, 그 뒤에 'the armies(군대)'를 놓아요: against → the → armies.

순서대로 이으면 mosquitoes / helped / protect / the / city / against / the / armies.
det.tip: help + 동사원형(protect) / against = ~로부터·~에 맞서

questions.wa: mosquitoes helped protect the city against the armies
accept: mosquitoes helped protect the city against the armies

questions.passage: Sharks, lions, or bears?  According to history professor Timothy Winegard, it is actually the mosquito.  __________ like malaria and yellow fever.  Over a million people worldwide die of these diseases every year.
questions.stem:
다음 우리말 뜻에 맞도록 주어진 단어를 모두 배열하여 문장을 완성하시오.

"모기는 치명적인 질병을 옮길 수 있다." (6단어) (영어로) [조건] (1) can, deadly, diseases, Mosquitoes, on, pass 를 모두 사용 (2) 정확히 6단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: Mosquitoes can pass on deadly diseases
det.analysis:
'모기는 ~할 수 있다'가 핵심이라 '주어(Mosquitoes) + 조동사(can)'로 시작해요: Mosquitoes → can.

조동사 can 뒤에는 동사원형을 써요. '옮기다'는 pass on이라는 두 단어 표현(구동사)이라 붙여서 놓아요: can → pass → on.

무엇을 옮기는가 하면 '치명적인 질병'이에요. 형용사가 명사를 앞에서 꾸미니 deadly(치명적인) → diseases(질병들) 순서예요: deadly → diseases.

순서대로 이으면 Mosquitoes / can / pass / on / deadly / diseases.
det.tip: can + 동사원형 / pass on = 옮기다·전달하다(구동사) / 형용사(deadly) + 명사(diseases)

questions.wa: Mosquitoes can pass on deadly diseases
accept: Mosquitoes can pass on deadly diseases
